AMGN.rationale: Amgen's operating fundamentals show genuine improvement — Q3'25 revenue grew +12.4% YoY to $9.56B, gross profit expanded +24.7%, and operating cash flow hit $4.68B (+31.2% YoY). However, the stock is extremely unattractive at current valuation. The PE has expanded from ~36x to ~45x over 12 months entirely on multiple re-rating, not durable earnings improvement. The 2.2% earnings yield is less than half the 4.34% risk-free rate, leaving no margin of safety. Earnings quality is clouded by volatile non-operating items (Q3'25 net income of $3.22B exceeded operating income of $2.53B, while Q2 showed the opposite pattern). The balance sheet carries $54.6B in debt on only $9.6B of equity (D/E ~8.0x), creating significant refinancing and rate risk. The denosumab patent cliff ($6B+ in combined Prolia/XGEVA sales) arrives in 2025-2026 before MariTide or next-gen assets can contribute, creating a probable growth deceleration. Q1 2026 earnings (Apr 30) are expected to show adjusted EPS down 3.1% YoY. The stock is priced for perfection at 44.7x PE with a 2.2% earnings yield against 4.34% risk-free, while facing patent cliffs, extreme leverage, and earnings quality concerns. All three pillars align negatively: deteriorating near-term earnings trajectory, stretched valuation vs own history, and a near-term downside catalyst (Q1 earnings miss risk).
